root_cause: Three defects in the fork's plain-C clip idiom patterns (RISCVInstrInfoXpulp.td, introduced in fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 [LLVM/PULP/SNITCH] Support for PULP and Snitch cores/platforms; found with git log pulp/integer_SIMD_fix -S'def betweenu' and -S'getZExtValue() == ~bound2'). (1) The bound leaves powerOf2Minus1_pulp/negativePowerOf2 are TImmLeaf, which matches only TargetConstant, while smin/smax operands are plain Constant. (2) The clip PatFrag predicate compared getZExtValue() with ~getZExtValue(): for i32 constants the upper 32 bits are zero, so ~ never equals the other bound. (3) The p.clipu idiom (betweenu) used umin/umax, but p.clipu compares signed (GVSoC lib_CLIPU: a>hi -> hi, a<=0 -> 0), and umax(x,0) is folded away before ISel. Missed optimization only; no miscompile before or after.
fix: New ImmLeaf leaves powerOf2Minus1_imm_pulp (isPowerOf2_32(Imm+1) && isUInt<30>) and negativePowerOf2_imm (capped at -2^30), so the encoded field is at most 31. The clip predicate uses getSExtValue. A new clipu_idiom PatFrags matches smin(smax(x,0),hi), smax(smin(x,hi),0) and umin(smax(x,0),hi). The existing trailing1sPlus1_pulp xform gives the immediate, as in upstream CORE-V (RISCVInstrInfoXCV.td:723 powerOf2Minus1 ImmLeaf, :771-773 trailing1sPlus1 @llvmorg-20.1.8). Upstream matches only the cv.clip intrinsic, not smin/smax idioms, at 20.1.8. Builtin patterns and register-form (p.clipr/p.clipur) patterns are unchanged.

other_errors_seen: PRE-EXISTING MISCOMPILE (codegen, insn-tablegen, not caused or changed by this task): the p.clipr idiom pattern `def : Pat<(between (not rs2), rs2, rs1), (P_CLIPR rs1, rs2)>` (RISCVInstrInfoXpulp.td, from f1b7aebff8c2) is only equivalent when rs2 >= 0. For a negative bound, p.clipr computes low=-rs2-1 > high=rs2 and lib_CLIP returns low for x<low, while smin(smax(x,~b),b) = b. Repro: logs/20-F008-v2/clipr/ (int rc(int x,int b){int t=x<~b?~b:x; return t>b?b:t;} with b=-5): int-20 and this build both emit p.clipr and give 5/8 wrong results on GVSoC (x=0 gives 4, expected -5). GAP9 GCC emits not+p.max+p.min. Suggested separate task: drop the idiom-to-p.clipr pattern or restrict it to a provably non-negative bound; keep the builtin clip_r pattern.

The p.clipur idiom pattern (betweenu rs2, rs1) uses unsigned min/max and is dead, because umax(x,0) folds away. If it ever matched, it would be wrong (p.clipur compares signed). Same separate task as p.clipr; not touched here.
